stories.title: Implement owned deadline-aware framed worker transport
changes: Private parent/child IPC adapter used by _ProcessWorker and _planner_worker_main; internal framing/read/write protocol; supervised transport fault fixtures
acceptance: After D02 approves the cancellation contract, use an owned socketpair/stream adapter (or a separately reviewed equivalent) with explicit length framing and parent-side nonblocking reads AND writes. Readiness never means a whole frame: accumulate header/body incrementally and wait for more bytes only through deadline/cancellation-aware selector slices. Do not call blocking Connection.recv(), send(), or sendall() on the coordinator after the deadline begins.

Preserve existing worker result types and external Kafka/plan formats. Specify frame-length/resource limits and clear failures for oversize, truncated, corrupt or EOF frames; document parent-side codec computation separately from bounded I/O waits without silently excluding post-submission IPC.

Own both endpoints in the planner; close duplicate child endpoints promptly. No receiver/helper thread or process is required by this design, so cancellation must not create an orphan helper. Parent broadcasts and stop delivery use the same bounded write path; if a child will not read stop, escalate through the separate cleanup budget instead of blocking on send.

Keep original initial submission/source-pickling exclusions explicit. Each advertised platform must support and test the chosen nonblocking socket transport; otherwise restrict that process-transport claim in D04. If implementation discovery needs a different ownership/transport design or exceeds this slice, split/re-review before coding.
validation: Test partial headers, partial bodies, frames larger than socket buffers, EOF/truncation and write backpressure on the private adapter with fake clocks/readiness controls; prove every wait rechecks its supplied cancellation signal and absolute deadline.

Use real-process private-adapter fixtures for a worker that begins a valid reply larger than the socket buffer, exposes partial readiness and stalls, and a worker that stops reading later commands/stop frames. Exercise transport-level signal/deadline exits for both receive and send; assert the private adapter reports its interruption/failure promptly. An external supervisor enforces an independent hard deadline and owns fixture child/endpoint cleanup so regressions cannot hang pytest.

This story gates private transport behavior and fixture ownership only. Public planner signatures/errors and partial-frame/backpressure integration controls are delivered by E04.F2.S3; complete operation elapsed-budget, liveness, marker and resource guarantees are gated by E04.F2.S4. Keep all negative controls in those successor gates.

stories.title: Implement bounded process-worker waits and cancellation
changes: Public planner/convenience API signatures; _ProcessWorker.recv and parent gather/broadcast waits; cancellation-contract.md
acceptance: Implement the D02-approved proposal in cancellation-contract.md: parent-only cancel_event and optional timeout_seconds, with distinct approved cancellation/timeout errors. If D02 selects a materially different design, revise this story before coding.

Integrate E04.F2.S5 complete-frame transport with parent gather/broadcast/result processing: bounded nonblocking I/O slices (target <=100 ms) check cancellation and the one absolute deadline during headers, bodies and write backpressure, not just before a blocking recv. Cancellation must not mutate caller start methods/signals.

Inline sources execute synchronously: cancellation/deadlines are cooperative between records/phases; arbitrary blocked next(), source construction, pickling, client callbacks or OS-uninterruptible work are explicitly outside interruption guarantees. Process mode is required when callers need to stop a blocked records() worker.

Use one operation-wide absolute monotonic deadline across all planning phases, never reset per gather/phase. Process-mode clock starts once initial task serialization/submission completes; inline-mode clock starts immediately before the first source iteration so the scan is included. Record it once and check between inline records. Kafka admin, source construction/pickling, arbitrary blocked next()/callbacks and OS-uninterruptible operations retain their explicitly documented exclusions.
validation: Through public imports, use a real child source that blocks after task submission plus deterministic fake-clock waits: cancellation/timeout is observed within poll tolerance; ordinary source errors retain their diagnostic cause.
Test cooperative inline cancellation and explicitly document/test the unsupported inline-blocking boundary; never write a test that waits forever to prove it.

Use fake clocks and a multi-phase source to prove expiry accumulates across scan/hub/emit rather than resetting; prove inline scan time is included from the first iteration and the process clock anchor is the completed initial submission.

With an inline source yielding ten individually returning records and advancing a fake monotonic clock on each record, assert a short timeout interrupts the scan before all ten records are consumed, not only after initial submission. Separately assert time between a completed process start() and later finish() counts toward the same stored deadline.

Through public planner imports, separately supervise real-process partial-large-reply stalls and later-command write backpressure, testing both cancellation and timeout. Assert the approved public error and prompt coordinator signal/deadline observation using the existing abort/terminate path. The supervisor has an independent hard deadline and owns emergency fixture cleanup; private-adapter tests alone do not satisfy this gate. E04.F2.S4 supplies the final total elapsed-budget, complete liveness, marker and resource assertions across these same public cases.

stories.title: Apply a bounded cleanup budget after cancellation/failure
changes: Worker close/terminate/kill paths; parent finally cleanup; output failure markers and owned spill state
acceptance: Define one overall cleanup deadline (proposed configurable internal 10-second budget, chosen/tested within D02) across supported workers rather than N unbounded joins; signal workers first, then bounded join/terminate/kill as supported by the approved platform.

For normal spawned Python workers a cancelled/expired operation raises its public error after bounded cleanup. If the OS cannot reap a worker, report its identity and retain potentially live spill/ownership resources rather than falsely deleting another active owner; do not claim universal termination of OS-uninterruptible work.
Topic/file ownership and failure markers remain correct on source error, partial startup, cancellation and timeout; all normal test workers terminate and resources are reclaimed.

Transport endpoint closure and stop messages inherit E04.F2.S5 ownership/bounded writes; never wait indefinitely for a partial reply or full stop socket. No transport helper is introduced. Include partially transmitted reply/command cases in cleanup proofs; preserve potentially live state if a worker cannot be reaped.
validation: Test <=4 representative spawned workers including a blocked source, partial startup and a termination-resistant fake process; assert poll+cleanup budget with tolerant wall-clock bounds.
For each advertised worker count/platform in E08, validate the shared budget and unresolved-resource diagnostics. Do not close the API gate on a documentation-only bounded-shutdown claim.

Complete the public integration controls from E04.F2.S3 with final error/diagnostic, total poll-plus-cleanup elapsed-budget, worker/endpoint liveness, absence of leaked helpers, failure-marker and retained/reclaimed owned-resource assertions. Cover pre-reply blocked source, mid-frame reply stall, later-command/stop write backpressure, ordinary source failure and partial startup; exercise both timeout and cancellation where applicable. Keep an independent hard-deadline supervisor with emergency cleanup, and prove normal children exit while an unreapable-worker fake retains potentially live resources and reports their identities.
